motion.name: camera-and-sheet

motion.name: dialog-entry

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Animations use 0.01ms; entries and sheet movement retain opacity transitions without travel or scale.

motion.name: loading-progress
motion.purpose: Existing loading progress synchronization; retain alongside settled sheet height/width motion.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: Pointer commands scale to 0.97; keyboard actions and list places stay still.

motion.name: popover
motion.purpose: Anchored scale(0.97) entry; masthead popovers close immediately.

motion.name: tooltip
motion.purpose: 500ms initial hover delay; instant entry for keyboard and a 300ms follow-on window; 150ms departure delay allows pointer travel.

Their 48px desktop minimum, 44px phone minimum, and automatic height allow enlarged labels to wrap. Browse scope stays neutral; task controls flow into the index without a rule. Short-landscape tabs retain natural full-label widths and set the side-sheet peek width.

narrative.overview:
A calm clinical workspace in light or dark around a dark imaging stage. The masthead states what data is loaded, one task panel explores and drills into it, and the stage carries only the tools that act on the picture. Keep the Planum name, the cut-away brain mark, and English and French copy.

This is a visual direction, not a clinical claim. Preserve the “not clinical anatomy” statement, scientific geometry, measurements, source labels, provenance, and published data colours. Panel theme and renderer keep independent palettes.
keyCharacteristics: Three homes: masthead = data, panel = modes, task controls and drill-in, stage = section and display tools.
One continuous workspace with a 24px desktop panel inset, compact neutral instruments before scientific facts, and one fine rule separating navigation from the stage.
Three button ranks, one segmented vocabulary, one disclosure, one chevron.
Flat surfaces; clear selected, focused, and disabled states.

Desktop uses a max(64px, 4rem) masthead, 384px task panel, and max(32px, 2rem) footer; compact workspaces at 801–1000px use a 336px rail and 16px panel inset. The masthead identity column aligns with the task panel edge.
The stage tool names the current preset or View after free rotation, reserves stable label width, and keeps functional-division and paint-key targets at least 44px on touch devices.
Phones and narrow windows at 800px and below use the responsive sheet shell; desktop workspaces at 801–1000px retain a 336px task rail.

Short-landscape grip selection and disclaimer occupy separate rows. The side sheet peek uses the tabs’ natural full-label width, and the top orientation letter remains 24px below the top-left scale bar.

rules.name: The Independent Palettes Rule
rules.body: UI teal communicates interaction. Tissue shading, atlas and network colours, streamline direction colours, outlines, orientation, and scale markings retain their scientific meaning in both themes.

rules.name: The Complete Name Rule
rules.body: Allow anatomical names and localized control labels to wrap. Prefer word boundaries; allow emergency wrapping when an anatomical name itself exceeds the panel at enlarged text sizes. Action rows wrap by content. Keep hemisphere labels explicit; truncate only compact selection readouts, the masthead summary's subject, and constrained navigation labels.

rules.name: The Flat Workspace Rule
rules.body: Use tonal surfaces and fine borders for the workspace. Reserve elevation for popovers and dialogs; segmented thumbs use only a subtle contact shadow.

dos: Do use the shared palette, spacing, typography, and radius tokens in viewer/styles/tokens.css.
Do keep data in the masthead, modes, task controls, and drill-in in the panel, and picture tools on the stage.
Do preserve visible focus, ARIA semantics, keyboard operation, and English and French at every breakpoint.
Do maintain readable hover, selected, disabled, empty, loading, and error states in both themes; text at least 4.5:1, field outlines and state edges at least 3:1.
Do verify UI changes in the browser and with the existing tests.
donts: Don’t recolour scientific data to match the UI accent or replace real anatomy with synthetic illustrations.
Don’t hide the “not clinical anatomy” statement in settings or add unsupported claims.
Don’t stack navigation rows: one location bar per detail view.
Don’t add a second filled button to a view, a new selected-state idiom, or a second disclosure style.
Don’t add decorative icon backgrounds, count badges, redundant controls, or ornamental motion.
